sections.heading: How to record your screen
sections.body:
Start on a desktop or laptop. The recorder runs in desktop browsers and does not run on phones. Then follow these steps:

1. Open [Screen Recorder](https://screen-recorder.lazur.app/) in Chrome, Edge or Firefox.
2. Choose what to record: your whole screen, one window, or one browser tab.
3. Turn on your microphone if you want your voice. Turn on tab or system audio if you want the sound from the source you picked.
4. Press record and wait for the 3-2-1 countdown.
5. Pause if you need a break. The timer shows how long the recording has run.
6. Stop the recording and download it as a WebM file.

Plan what should be on screen before you press record. That part matters more than the controls.

sections.heading: Pick the right source
sections.body:
You choose the source before the recording starts. Each choice works for a different job.

- **Whole screen:** use it when you show several apps, a desktop, or a process that moves between windows.
- **One window:** use it when one app is the focus. Other windows stay out of the picture.
- **One browser tab:** use it for a web page, an online course, a slide deck or a video that plays in that tab.

Make sure the right window or tab is picked before you press record. If the wrong one is picked, the file will show it, and you will have to record again.

sections.heading: Sound is optional
sections.body:
Audio is a separate choice from the picture. The microphone captures your voice from the mic your computer uses. Tab or system audio captures the sound from the source you picked, such as a video that plays in a tab. Which sound can be shared depends on your browser and on the source, so test a short clip if the sound matters to you.

Turn on only the audio you need. A microphone that is always on picks up fan noise, keyboard clicks and people in the room. Tab audio can add music or alerts you did not plan to use.

sections.heading: Countdown, pause and timer
sections.body:
The 3-2-1 countdown gives you a few seconds to get your hands and your screen ready. Use that time to close notifications and move the mouse out of the way.

Pause when you need to stop talking or switch tasks, then carry on. The timer shows the length of the recording so far, which helps you plan a short demo or a longer tutorial.

sections.heading: Where it works
sections.body: The recorder runs in desktop Chrome, Edge and Firefox. It does not run on phones, so use a computer for this job. If you are on a phone, look for the screen recorder built into the phone itself. On your computer, use the browser you already have open, and there is nothing to install.

sections.heading: Your recording stays with you
sections.body:
There is no watermark on your recording. You do not need an account or a sign-up to start. Nothing is uploaded, so the recording stays on your computer until you download it. You download the finished video as a WebM file and decide where it goes next.

For a specific job, open the page that matches it: [audio](https://screen-recorder.lazur.app/audio), [PC](https://screen-recorder.lazur.app/pc), [Chromebook](https://screen-recorder.lazur.app/chromebook), [YouTube](https://screen-recorder.lazur.app/youtube), [Zoom](https://screen-recorder.lazur.app/zoom), or [black screen fixes](https://screen-recorder.lazur.app/recording-black).

sections.heading: Set your audio before you record
sections.body:

- **Microphone:** your voice, from the mic your computer uses.
- **Tab or system audio:** the sound from the source you picked, such as a video or a call playing on your computer, where your browser can share it.
- **Both:** your voice on top of the sound from the screen. This suits tutorials, product demos and reactions.

Turn on only what you need. A microphone that is always on picks up fan noise, keyboard clicks and people in the room. Tab audio can add music or alerts you did not plan to use, so mute the sources you do not want before you start.

sections.heading: How to record screen and voice
sections.body:
Follow these steps for a narrated recording:

1. Open [Screen Recorder](https://screen-recorder.lazur.app/) in a desktop browser.
2. Turn the microphone on.
3. Turn tab or system audio on if the sound you need comes from the screen.
4. Pick the source. For a demo, choose the window you are showing.
5. Press record, let the 3-2-1 countdown finish, and start talking.
6. Stop the recording and download the WebM file.

Before a long take, record a 10-second test. Download it and play it back on your computer. If your voice is quiet, or the sound from the screen is too loud, fix it now. That is much faster than finding out after 20 minutes of recording.

sections.heading: When the sound from the screen is missing
sections.body:
Whether sound from your screen is recorded depends on the browser and on the source you pick. Browsers differ in what they can share, so the same test may give different results in two browsers.

If the file has your voice but no other sound, try the same test again with a browser tab as the source, and play a short clip of audio in that tab first. If the sound is still missing, your browser is not sharing it for that source. Try another browser, or pick a different source for the recording.

If the picture is black as well as silent, read the [black screen fixes](https://screen-recorder.lazur.app/recording-black) page.

sections.heading: Privacy of your audio
sections.body: Nothing is uploaded. Your voice and the sound from the screen stay on your computer until you download the file, and there is no account to link them to. A recording with audio can also pick up people nearby, so check the room before you press record and close the door if someone is talking in the next room.

faq.q: Can I record my screen and voice at the same time?
faq.a: Yes. Turn on the microphone before you press record. Your voice is recorded together with the screen, so you do not need a second app for narration.

faq.q: Does an online screen recorder record system sound?
faq.a: It can, where your browser offers it for the source you pick. Choose tab or system audio before you press record, then record a short test and play it back. If the sound is missing, the browser is not sharing that audio for this source.

faq.q: Is an online screen recorder with audio free?
faq.a: Yes. This recorder is free, adds no watermark and needs no sign-up. You can record a screen with your voice, tab audio or both, then download the file as WebM.

faq.q: Why is my screen recording silent?
faq.a: Check the microphone and audio choices before you press record. Then record 10 seconds, download the file and play it back. If it is still silent, pick a different source, such as a browser tab, and test again.

sections.heading: Desktop only, no phones

faq.q: How do I screen record on my PC with sound?

faq.q: Can I record my PC screen for free?

pages.title: Screen Recorder Recording Black Screen: Fixes | Lazur
pages.description: Recording a black screen? See the usual causes, including protected video, and how to pick a source that records. Free, in your browser, no sign-up.
pages.claim: A black recording usually means the source gave the recorder no picture, or the video is protected. Pick a visible tab or window and record a short test. Protected video from streaming services usually stays black in any browser recorder.

sections.heading: Why the picture is black
sections.body:
A recorder can only capture what the browser shares with it. A black file usually comes from one of three things:

- **The video is protected.** Streaming services and some paid courses mark their video as protected. Browsers usually do not let recorders capture that picture, so it comes out black. This recorder cannot capture it either.
- **The source gave no picture.** A window that is minimized, hidden behind another window or closed can record as black.
- **The graphics layer is in the way.** On some laptops with two graphics chips, or when a browser uses hardware acceleration, the picture may not reach the share. Restarting the browser sometimes clears it.

The fix depends on which one is happening. Start with the source, because that is the quickest check.

sections.heading: Fix a black recording, step by step
sections.body:
1. Close the recording and make sure the window or tab you want is open and visible on your screen.
2. Restart the browser, so the sharing starts fresh.
3. Open [Screen Recorder](https://screen-recorder.lazur.app/) again and choose a browser tab that shows the content. Tabs are the most direct source.
4. Record for 10 seconds, stop, and download the file.
5. Play the file. If the picture is there, record the full take.

If the test is still black, try a different browser. If every source is black, the video you want to record is most likely protected, and the steps above will not change that.

sections.heading: When the video is from a streaming service
sections.body:
Streaming services and many paid courses use protected video. In a recording, a black frame then usually means the browser blocked the picture. It does not mean the recorder is broken. Trying more sources will not change that result.

Use the recorder for your own content instead: slides, code, a product demo, a sketch or a web page you built. Record only what you have the right to record, and follow the terms of the service you are using.

sections.heading: When the picture is fine but the sound is not
sections.body:
The picture and the sound are separate choices. A recording can show the screen clearly and still have no sound. If that is your problem, read the [audio page](https://screen-recorder.lazur.app/audio), which explains microphone and tab audio and how to test them.

If you need a recording with a second person speaking on a call, the [Zoom page](https://screen-recorder.lazur.app/zoom) has notes on testing sound before the call.

sections.heading: Check before a long recording
sections.body:
A long recording that turns out black wastes the whole session. Always run a 10-second test with the same source and the same browser you plan to use. Download the test clip and play it back. Only after the picture shows up should you start the full take.

The recorder keeps nothing on a server, so the test clip is only on your computer. Delete it once you have checked it.

faq.q: How to get around black screen when screen recording?
faq.a: Protected video is usually blocked from browser recorders, so there is no workaround for that video here. For your own content, pick a visible tab or window, restart the browser, and record a 10-second test. If the picture appears, record the full take.

faq.q: How to fix black screen in video?
faq.a: A black screen is in the file because the recorder got no picture, so editing rarely fixes it. Record again with the right source. A video editor can crop or trim a clip, but it cannot add picture that was never captured.

faq.q: Why is my screen recording black?
faq.a: It is usually one of three things: a protected video, a window that is hidden or minimized, or a graphics problem. Choose a visible tab or window, restart the browser, and test for 10 seconds before the full take.

sections.heading: Record a YouTube video in a tab

Play the first 10 seconds before you start the full take, then download and check the picture and the sound.

sections.heading: Why tab audio matters

A YouTube video is picture and sound together. Tab audio is what carries the video's sound into the recording. If you pick a window instead of the tab, the sound may not come along, since browsers differ in what they can share for each source.

If the picture is fine and the sound is missing, pick the tab again with tab audio on and record a 10-second test. The [audio page](https://screen-recorder.lazur.app/audio) explains the choices in more detail.

sections.heading: Get the tab ready before you record
sections.body: Open the video and let it load before you press record. Close other tabs that play sound, such as music or a call, so their sound does not mix into the tab audio. Then start the recording and the video together, so the file opens on the first frame you want to keep.

sections.heading: Pause around ads and breaks
sections.body: Pausing the recording lets you skip the ads without leaving them in the file. Press pause before an ad starts, and resume when the video is back. Check the file after the first recording, to make sure the pauses fell where you wanted them.

sections.heading: Only record what you may keep

sections.heading: Record a Zoom meeting in your browser
sections.body:
The recorder captures the window or tab where the meeting runs. Follow these steps:

1. Open the meeting on your computer, either in the Zoom app or in a browser tab.
2. Open [Screen Recorder](https://screen-recorder.lazur.app/) in Chrome, Edge or Firefox.
3. Turn on the microphone to capture your voice.
4. Turn on tab or system audio to capture the meeting sound, if your browser offers it for the source you pick.
5. Choose the Zoom window, or the tab that holds the meeting.
6. Press record, let the countdown finish, and join or continue the meeting.
7. Stop the recording when the meeting ends and download the WebM file.

The recorder cannot see inside Zoom. It records the picture and sound of the source you chose, so pick the right one before you press record.

sections.heading: Choose the right window for the meeting
sections.body:
Pick the window or tab that shows the speakers, so the file is about the meeting. If you want the chat in the file too, record the whole screen instead, with the chat where you can see it.

Move the meeting window to the screen you will record before you press record, and close the windows you do not want to show. A window that moves during the recording may end up cut off in the file.

sections.heading: Test the sound before the meeting
sections.body:
Whether the meeting sound is included depends on the source you pick and on your browser. Run a 10-second test before the meeting: record, download the clip, and play it back. Check that the other people's voices are in the clip, not only yours.

If the other voices are missing, pick a different source, such as the browser tab that holds the meeting, and test again. The [audio page](https://screen-recorder.lazur.app/audio) explains the choices in more detail.

sections.heading: Tell people before you record
sections.body:
Tell everyone on the call before you start, and ask the host whether the meeting rules allow recording. Many meetings have their own rules about it, and the host sets them.

The recorder cannot tell who is on the call or what the rules are. That check is yours to make.

sections.heading: What the recording shows
sections.body:
The recording shows whatever is in the source you chose. If you pick a whole screen, other windows, notifications and private tabs can appear in the file. A single window keeps the picture to the meeting. Close anything private before you start.

When you are done, play the file once from start to finish. Check the picture, the sound and anything that should not be there.

sections.heading: Privacy and files
sections.body: Nothing is uploaded. The meeting recording stays on your computer as a WebM file that you download. Store it somewhere you control, and delete it when you no longer need it.

faq.q: Can I record a Zoom meeting using a screen recorder?
faq.a: Yes. Choose the Zoom window or the tab with the meeting, turn on your mic and tab audio, and press record. Whether the meeting sound is included depends on the source and your browser, so test first.

faq.q: How can I record a Zoom meeting online?
faq.a: Open this recorder in a desktop browser, choose the Zoom window or tab, turn on audio, and press record. Stop when the meeting ends and download the WebM file. Tell the others before you start.

faq.q: Is there a free screen recorder for Zoom meetings?
faq.a: Yes. This recorder is free, adds no watermark and needs no sign-up. It captures the window or tab you choose in a desktop browser, and nothing is uploaded.

faq.q: Can I record a Zoom meeting I am not hosting?
faq.a: You can record your own screen, but the host's rules and the people on the call decide whether recording is allowed. Ask the host and tell everyone before you press record.
